answer: Identity verification uses a Wesolowski verifiable delay function: each candidate identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before producing a compact proof. GPUs may run separate chains concurrently, but cannot split one chain to bypass its dependency-bound delay, so each Sybil clone incurs its own real-time cost. The relic of a prior round, a vertex in the identity graph, or a vault of proofs cannot substitute for that computation.
